title: fix(plugin-hono-server): keep a graceful close from cutting off a response still flushing to a slow client
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X6PYHRe3yiUSd4YRysSoxcj)_

Fixes #31208

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:服务优雅关闭(`HonoHttpServer.close()`)时,一个已经调用 `end()`、但还在往慢客户端发送的响应,不再在关闭开始那一刻被掐断;空闲的 keep-alive 连接改为在没有响应仍在发送时才统一释放。
- 为什么改:每次 `os serve` / 运行时关停或重新部署时,正在下载大响应的客户端会收到被截断的内容(实测 32 MiB 只收到 3,919,702 字节),原因是 Node 自己的 `server.close()` 把「已 end 未发完」的连接当作空闲连接销毁了。
- 风险与回滚:只改 `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` 一个文件,patch 级;关闭窗口的强制关闭兜底(默认 10 秒)原样保留,所以最坏情况是空闲连接晚一点释放,不会让关停卡住;回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts` 的 `closeIdleConnectionsOnceFlushed`(什么时候推迟清扫),再看 `tryListen` 里把它装到 server 实例上的那三行,以及 `trackForDrain` 里响应 `'close'` 时补跑被推迟的清扫。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server exec vitest run src/adapter-drain.test.ts`,预期 9 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`, the drain start of `HonoHttpServer.close()`:

- **What destroyed the response, measured.** On Node 22.23.4 (`.nvmrc` is `22`, `engines` is `>=22.0.0`, and every CI job reads `.nvmrc` or pins `'22'`), a `Socket.prototype.destroy` probe during the reordered slow-reader case recorded two destroys of the flushing socket, in this order: first `Server.closeIdleConnections` called from `httpServerPreClose` from `Server.close` (`adapter.ts` `server.close(...)`), then the adapter's own `server.closeIdleConnections()` call on the next line. So Node's own `server.close()` sweep destroys it first; the adapter's call would have done the same. Both skip a connection only while `socket._httpMessage.finished` is false, and `end()` sets `finished` before the bytes are flushed.
- **The guard.** `tryListen` puts a `closeIdleConnections` on the server instance that wraps Node's: `closeIdleConnectionsOnceFlushed` runs Node's sweep only when no tracked response is `writableEnded && !writableFinished`. Otherwise it holds the sweep back. Node's `httpServerPreClose` calls `server.closeIdleConnections()` on the instance (the probe's stack shows it), so both sweeps at drain start go through the guard, and `server.close()` still stops accepting and clears Node's connection-check interval at once.
- **Each flushing connection closes after its own `'finish'`.** That path is PR #31189's, unchanged: the response's `'close'` `destroySoon()`s its own socket once it has finished and nothing else is owed on that connection.
- **The held-back sweep then runs.** Each tracked response's `'close'` (in `trackForDrain`) re-asks the guard when a sweep is held back, so idle keep-alive connections are released as soon as no response is flushing, not a keep-alive window later. Node's raw server-wide sweep is still never run from a response's `'close'` (the PR #31189 M1 hazard): the only sweep there is the guarded one, which runs only when nothing is flushing.
- **The backstop is untouched.** The `closeAllConnections()` timer and its window are byte-identical. A reader that never drains is now held until the window ends instead of being destroyed at drain start.

**Why this route and not the other one the card names.** Stopping the accept without the sweep means calling `net.Server.prototype.close` instead of `server.close()`. That skips the other half of `httpServerPreClose`, `clearInterval(server[kConnectionsCheckingInterval])`, an interval only reachable through a private symbol, so it would keep the closed server alive in a timer; and calling `server.close()` later to clear it emits `'close'` a second time when the connections have already drained. Deferring the whole `server.close()` keeps accepting new connections during the flush. The instance guard keeps Node's `close()` whole and changes only when its sweep runs, on every Node the CI runs (22) and any with the sweep (19 and later).

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter-drain.test.ts`, three new cases:

- **The reordered slow-reader pin.** A 32 MiB response calls `end()` to a paused raw socket before `close()` starts; the case asserts the premise (`writableEnded` true, `writableFinished` false), then the client receives every byte against `Content-Length`. An idle keep-alive connection sits beside it and must be released within 1 s of the flush ending (the keep-alive timer would hold it 5 s). **Red on `main`** (`df22adc3`, adapter unchanged since `714dda8f`): `every byte of the body arrived: expected 3919702 to be 33554432`.
- **Control: an idle keep-alive connection is released at drain start.** Nothing is flushing, so the sweep runs at once: `close()` and the connection end within 1 s.
- **Control: the backstop still force-closes a reader that never drains.** A paused reader of a 32 MiB response with a 300 ms window: `close()` takes at least 250 ms (held for the window, not swept at drain start) and under 2 s, and the reader gets fewer than 32 MiB.

<details><summary>Ablations</summary>

Through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed head, anchor hit once, restore proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The suite imports `./adapter` from `src/`, so no build sits on the path.

- A1 (head `ab2845c8`), the guard's flushing check disabled (`if (false && res.writableEnded && !res.writableFinished)`): 2 failed / 7 passed. `a response that ended before close() but is still flushing to a slow reader arrives whole`: `expected 3919702 to be 33554432`; `the drain window still force-closes a reader that never drains`: `expected 1 to be greater than or equal to 250`.
- A2 (head `1502afc5`), the held-back sweep never re-run (the `if (sweep) this.closeIdleConnectionsOnceFlushed(sweep);` line deleted): 1 failed / 8 passed, the slow-reader case `Test timed out in 5000ms` (the idle keep-alive connection holds `close()` open).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The guard relies on Node calling the instance method.** `httpServerPreClose` reads `server.closeIdleConnections()` dynamically in Node 22 (measured by the probe's stack). If a future Node called the prototype directly, the slow-reader pin goes red again; it does not fail silently.
- **Idle connections wait while something flushes.** While an ended response is still flushing, the sweep is held back, so an idle keep-alive connection stays open until the flush ends (then it is released at once) or the window ends. A request arriving on it meanwhile is answered `Connection: close` by PR #31189's request-time line. Under a stream of new slow flushes the backstop decides, as before.
- **A pipelined response queued behind another counts as flushing once it has ended** (its bytes sit in `outputData`), which only holds the sweep back until it is written. A dead connection's responses drop out with the connection's entry, so they cannot hold the sweep.
